There's always been a lot of overlap between BWF and Boxing training, and I've always been a fan of both old-school and new-school boxing. So I've taken two popular old-timey drills, modified them to be more about conditioning than skill, and now I'm giving them to you. So, without further ado, I'll share two old-school boxing drills that I'm quite fond of. You'll need a length of rope and two mount points for the first one, and you'll need a heavy bag and gloves for the second one.

  1. Slip Rope training/ Rope Weaving To do this, you'll need a length of rope in your training area, stretching about ten feet so you have room to work. Mount it at about shoulder height, lower if you're highly mobile. Bob and weave (or, in layman's turns, squat under it) coming up quickly on the opposite side, while throwing a punch. Uppercuts are best for conditioning. Repeat quickly,either staying in place or moving forward. I suggest 3 rounds of 3 minutes. Jack Dempsey built a 5-foot high cage to practice drills in, but he also chewed wood chips and bathed in brine, so maybe he's not the world's best role model.

  2. Out-of-Plumb Sprints- You'll need a heavy bag, boxing gloves, and preferably hand wraps (This arguably isn't bodyweight work, but you're not really using barbells either, so I'll add it.). If you don't think you can break your hand punching the bag without gloves, you can't punch for shit and should be out working on that. For the rest of you, this drill is fairly simple. Lean your head against the heavy bag until it's slightly out of alignment with the ground. Then keep it out of alignment by punching it. 30 to 60 second burst are good for this one. To make it harder, make sure you're punches are "snapping" the bag, rather than pushing it. This forces you to retract your punches faster and use better form. Alternatively you can widen the angle, either keeping the bag farther away or by stepping back and throwing longer punches.

Thanks for reading my descriptions, if you need a more detailed description feel free to ask, and if you need more /v/amateurboxing has some good stuff in there. Stay strong brothers. /u/agitprop out.
